prompt: Please finish the configuration migration in this service. Every settings caller outside `third_party/` must use the interface in `lib/config.js`, whose `value` entry takes a section, a key, and an options object with a `fallback` field. Preserve each module's returned settings and its derived value against the fixed data in `config/app.json`. Remove `lib/conf.js`, remove the old `read` export from `lib/index.js`, and update its settings export to use the current interface. Refresh the old-reader wording in `README.md` and `docs/config.md`. Leave `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/operations.md`, and `config/app.json` intact. Keep `config/app.json` as valid JSON, keep the CommonJS module format, leave every byte under `third_party/` unchanged, and keep all existing files in `test/*.test.js` passing. Do not add packages or change unrelated behavior.

checks.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('node:fs'); const text=fs.readFileSync('README.md','utf8')+fs.readFileSync('docs/config.md','utf8'); if(/conf\.read/i.test(text)) process.exit(1); const files=[]; function walk(d){for(const n of fs.readdirSync(d)){if(d==='.'&&n==='third_party') continue; const p=d==='.'?n:d+'/'+n; if(fs.statSync(p).isDirectory()) walk(p); else if(p.endsWith('.js')) files.push(p);}} walk('.'); const requirePattern=/require\s*\(\s*(['\"])([^'\"]+)\1\s*\)/g; if(files.some(p=>{const source=fs.readFileSync(p,'utf8'); return [...source.matchAll(requirePattern)].some(match=>{const target=match[2]; return target==='conf' || target.endsWith('/conf') || target.endsWith('/conf.js');});})) process.exit(1);"

rubric.criterion: The documentation explains the current settings interface in terms that an operator can apply. Fail: README.md or docs/config.md still describes conf.read as the way to read settings, or says nothing usable about config.value. Partial: both files name config.value, but leave out how a dotted key becomes a section and a key, or how the fallback behaves. Pass: both files describe config.value(section, key, { fallback }) with a worked example, how a key with more than two parts is split, and that the fallback applies only when the value is missing, and neither presents the removed reader as current. (code cannot check this because execution cannot judge whether prose is clear to its intended reader)

Every migrated call passes the section and the key the way lib/config.js defines them (the first dotted part is the section, the rest is the key). Fail: callers keep their own splitter, hard-code a flattened key, or pass a three-part key whole as the section. Partial: most callers are right, but a key with more than two parts, or the dispatch and queue region keys, is passed in a different shape in one or two files. Pass: every caller outside third_party/ calls config.value(section, key, ...) with the documented split, including every key with more than two parts and the region keys, and none re-implements the split. (code cannot check this because tests compare results against fixed data, so a caller that returns the right value by another path still passes)

Each caller's old default now goes through the fallback option. Fail: callers add a default after the call with || or ??, or drop the default so a missing value returns undefined. Partial: the fallback option is used, but a falsy value (0, an empty string, false) is replaced by a default in one or two callers. Pass: every default is passed as { fallback }, falsy values read from config/app.json are kept, and no caller adds its own default after the call. (code cannot check this because a test sees the returned value, not whether the default came from the interface or from the caller)

The retired reader is gone without side effects. Fail: lib/conf.js, the read export or a require of the old reader is still present. Partial: the code is clean, but a comment, an unused import or a doc line still names the old reader, or an unrelated file was reformatted. Pass: lib/conf.js and the read export are removed, lib/index.js exports the current interface, nothing in the code or the docs names the old reader as current, and the diff touches no unrelated file. (code cannot check this because a test checks that the reader is missing, not whether leftovers or unrelated edits remain)

verdicts.note: The request asks to migrate callers to config.value() interface without naming specific methods or traps. It only specifies the interface signature and what files to modify.

Fixed in the author's fix round: the request now says the old read export goes away from lib/index.js; 'derived value' is each module's own computed field, which the fixture modules return and the request says to preserve. (reviewer: The request says 'preserve each module's returned settings and its derived value against the fixed data in config/app.json' but doesn't specify what 'derived value' means. However, tests in lib/audit-prefix.js show modules calling read() from lib/index.js, which the fixture exports with both read and value. The hidden tests reveal callers expect the old read interface in lib/index.js, but the request doesn't clarify whether lib/index.js.read should be removed or preserved.)

The caller table lives in the hidden test, which the agent never sees; nothing in the fixture lists the expected calls. (reviewer: The hidden-behaviour.test.js contains callerTable with 62 caller modules and their exact expected calls to config.value(section, key, {fallback}). This reveals the precise migration pattern (e.g., how dotted keys split into section/key, how queue modules use runtime region). Comments in the hidden test itself also reveal the answer about queue callers needing runtime region in the key.)

The reviewer's own note shows a quick answer passes 1 of 10 hidden tests; the dry run scores the plain fixture 7.1 and the lazy answer 14.3. (reviewer: A quick wrong answer would be to just change require('./conf') to require('./config') and call config.value() without properly transforming the dotted keys or handling runtime region for queue callers. Test '#0 tests' in selfcheck shows this would only pass 1/10 hidden tests (the simple ones like config.value with static keys).)

The fixture's callers read the setting when called, so a behaviour-preserving change keeps reading it at run time; the queue modules already take the region as an argument. The worker's own floor finding (a docs check that failed the words legacy or old reader) was fixed in the fix round. (reviewer: The hidden test '#5 caller results respond to a changed reader value' monkey-patches config.value() and expects callers to call it dynamically. This cannot be derived from the request or fixture—users must infer that config.value must be called at runtime, not pre-computed. The fixture's jobs/eu-queue.js uses `queues.${region}.url` as a template literal in conf.read(), but the test expects region to be a runtime parameter passed to the function, not a compile-time constant.)
